newsitem.title: UK: Crude oil tanker rates higher for Suezmax vessels.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil tanker rates higher for Suezmax vessels.

text.p: Demand for Suezmax tonnage from Western load areas raised rates on most routes while the closure of some ports in the Mediterranean by bad weather threatened to hold up vessels waiting to unload and supported Aframax rates in the region, brokers said.
Wednesday's fixtures saw at least five Suezmax vessels fixed from West Africa, which brokers said was the only animated area in an otherwise lacklustre tanker market.

"West Africa is the only area with any life. Suezmax from all Western load areas is very active, from the North Sea, West Africa, the Med and the Black Sea. There is an abundance of cargoes in all areas," a shipping broker said.
"This combination is allowing owners to pick and choose, which is not often the case. They are in the driving seat," he added.
Tonnage from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf for one million barrel business rose to W102.5, up from Tuesday's W97.5. A Suezmax booked from Hound Point to Philadelphia was fixed at a high W107.5.
The VLCC market was steady with modern ships fetching W65 for the Mideast/Far East and older ships having to take a discount of 7.5 points.
"There have been very few VLCCs fixed to the West. There is no change and the market is trundling along," the broker said.

The Caribbean market was static where an overabundance of tonnage put the brake on rates. A fixture for 50,000 tonne business into the U.S. Gulf at W147.5 was seen as an exception at 2.5 points above Tuesday's business for the same route.

Aframax business in the Med was quiet but brokers were waiting to see whether port closures would tighten availability of 80,000 tonne carriers. A Med broker said the Italian port of Fiumicino was closed nearly a week ago and vessels were unable to enter or leave Genoa because of bad weather conditions.
Algeria's Skikda port was also closed.
Black Sea and Sidi Kreir loadings were seen around W97.5-W105, higher than previous levels.
"With this bad weather, there will be some delays so you might see some shortage of vessels and the market might firm," the Med broker said.

Fuel oil tanker rates also rose for Inter/UKC business with 25,000 tonne cargoes fetching up to W190 because of higher Russian fuel oil exports, brokers said. Cross-Med business for same size vessels also rose 10 points to W180.
